newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - APN says still interested in Fairfax.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - APN says still interested in Fairfax.

text.p: Australian Provincial Newspapers Holdings Ltd is still interested in becoming part of any bid for newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, chief executive Cameron O'Reilly said on Wednesday.
"We were obviously interested at one time and we are still obviously very interested in Fairfax," O'Reilly told a business breakfast meeting.
However, O'Reilly said that if APN were to get involved in Fairfax there were "one or two big players who are interested at the moment and they have a head start in shareholdings."
"My own feeling is we'd never rule out an opportunity but it's not priority," O'Reilly said in reply to a question about whether APN was still interested in Fairfax.
He said if an opportunity arose from a change in regulations on media ownership "we'd certainly have a look at it."

APN, which is mainly involved in regional newspapers and radio stations, was part of a consortium several years ago which lost out in a bid for Fairfax to interests associated with Canadian media magnate Conrad Black.
Black's interests now hold a 25 percent stake in Fairfax.
O'Reilly, speaking at a breakfast meeting sponsored by Morgan Stockbroking, said APN was interested in expanding its regional newspapers division but there were few opportunities.
In specialist publishing, he said the group was focussing on Asia where he said it was easier to get a market foothold.

In broadcasting, he said: "There is not much that we can buy." However, he said that in the New Zealand radio market where the group had a 50 percent market share, APN might buy and sell some stations in the current year.
He said the New Zealand operations also may look for growth in Asia in the medium term.
"Over the next three to four years, I think we will broaden our base," he said. "You don't know where the next opportunity is coming from. Things are not aways what they seem."
